persona: Buyer for an online t-shirt shop who decides what sells

designs.why: The idea works: a nautical line drawing on a white tee in black ink is a reliable seller, and the hull, water and reflection look good from 3 m. The letter-spaced heading looks tidy too. But at $50 it has to look better than the generic sailboat tees that sell for $25, and the rig lets it down. The sails pile on top of each other in a tangle with no clearly drawn mainsail and boom, so it does not read as a proper ketch, and that is a problem under a heading that says 'Sail plan'. Sailors, the people most likely to buy this, will spot it. Up close (in the full-size crops) the dotted seams are blobby, uneven dashes that look like a degraded auto-trace, not fine pen work. On the model the light sail lines fade into the white cotton, so all that reads is a small dark hull with grey scribble above it.
designs.fix: Redraw the rig as a clean, correct ketch: a main and a mizzen, each with its boom, plus a jib and staysail, with sails that don't overlap. Use one even, fine line weight with small, regular seam dots, so the sail area reads as crisp engraving from a distance and stands up to close inspection.
